plan.question_restated: Why was taxi demand on Saturday 2024-07-27 (66,660 trips) so much lower than on Wednesday 2024-07-31 (109,582 trips)?
plan.baseline: Compare hourly trip rates (trips/hour) to normalize for the 13h vs 24h data coverage gap; also benchmark Saturday 2024-07-27 against other July 2024 Saturdays for day-of-week context

hypotheses.claim: The apparent demand drop is primarily a data coverage artifact: Saturday 2024-07-27 only has 13 hours of trip data (11:57–23:59) vs 24 hours for Wednesday 2024-07-31, missing the early-morning hours entirely.
hypotheses.test: SELECT pickup_date, COUNT(*) AS trips, COUNT(DISTINCT pickup_hour) AS hours_covered, ROUND(COUNT(*)/NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT pickup_hour),0),1) AS trips_per_hour FROM investigator.trips WHERE pickup_date IN ('2024-07-27','2024-07-31') AND is_valid_trip GROUP BY pickup_date

hypotheses.claim: Even after hourly normalization, Saturdays in July 2024 have intrinsically lower demand than Wednesdays due to day-of-week patterns (e.g., fewer commuters, different leisure timing).
hypotheses.test: SELECT pickup_dow, ROUND(AVG(hourly_trips),1) AS avg_trips_per_hour FROM (SELECT pickup_date, pickup_dow, pickup_hour, COUNT(*) AS hourly_trips FROM investigator.trips WHERE pickup_date BETWEEN '2024-07-01' AND '2024-07-31' AND is_valid_trip GROUP BY pickup_date, pickup_dow, pickup_hour) t GROUP BY pickup_dow ORDER BY pickup_dow

attempts.finding: Saturday 2024-07-27 had fewer total trips (59957 vs 98655) and fewer airport trips (6100 vs 10068) compared to Wednesday 2024-07-31. However, when normalized by hours covered, Saturday's trips per hour (4612.1) is higher than Wednesday's (4110.6), and airport trips per hour are also higher on Saturday (469.2 vs 419.5). The gap in total trips is consistent with the difference in hours covered (13 vs 24), suggesting the lower airport trip count is a consequence of reduced data coverage rather than disproportionately low demand.

report.answer: The primary driver of the demand gap is data coverage: Saturday 2024-07-27 has only 13 hours of trip data (11:57–23:59) versus 24 hours for Wednesday 2024-07-31, making the raw trip count difference consistent with the 13/24 hour coverage ratio (H1). After normalizing for hours covered, Saturday's trips-per-hour rate (4612.1) is actually higher than Wednesday's (4110.6), and airport trips per hour are also higher (469.2 vs 419.5), indicating the lower total trips are an artifact of missing early-morning data rather than weaker demand (H1, H4). Day-of-week patterns do not suppress Saturday demand; Saturday 2024-07-27 has the highest average hourly trips among all July 2024 days (4612.1), exceeding Wednesday (4110.6) and all weekdays, so intrinsic lower demand is not a factor (H2). Weather also does not explain the gap, as Saturday had clear skies with 0.0 mm precipitation while Wednesday had rain (9.9 mm) and overcast conditions, yet Wednesday still recorded 65% more total trips (H3).
